question: During ventricular systole:

options.opb: Intraventricular pressure is equal in both ventricles.
options.opc: The ventricular volume begins to decrease from the beginning of the contraction.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "The atria are relaxed" -> "The atrio-ventricular valves are open" -> "Ventricular volume begins to decrease from the beginning of the contraction" -> "Intraventricular pressure is equal in both ventricles" -> "All ventricular blood is expelled" -> 95%
enhanced_information: During ventricular systole, the atria are relaxed, allowing the atrio-ventricular valves to open. This leads to a decrease in ventricular volume from the beginning of the contraction. As a result, intraventricular pressure becomes equal in both ventricles, facilitating the expulsion of all ventricular blood. Evidence supports the manifestation of this process in the heart ventricles.
analysis: During ventricular systole, the atria are relaxed, allowing the atrio-ventricular valves to open, leading to a decrease in ventricular volume from the beginning of the contraction. This process results in intraventricular pressure becoming equal in both ventricles, facilitating the expulsion of all ventricular blood. Therefore, the most likely correct option is that the ventricular volume begins to decrease from the beginning of the contraction.
